bug_description.normalized: The exact staged reproducing checkout is metadata vulnerable commit `1a0e61510bd3b12463d1536d0b320d62bc23bec2`. The staged 27-byte witness is a text matrix file whose first line is the valid header `1 9\n`, so `vips_image_new_from_file()` selects `matrixload` and `vips_foreign_load_matrix_header()` admits `width = 1`, `height = 9`. During the later `vips_foreign_load_matrix_load()` row loop, `vips_sbuf_get_line_copy()` copies a later one-token non-digit row from the attacker-controlled file into heap buffer `line`; the witness contains such rows as the single bytes `0xc0` and `0x12`. The loop sets `p` to that in-place token, `vips_strtod(p, &matrix->linebuf[x])` fails, and the vulnerable error path immediately executes `g_free(line)` before `vips_error(class->nickname, _( "bad number \"%s\"" ), p)`. Because `p` still aliases bytes inside the freed row buffer, `vips_verror()` forwards a dangling `%s` argument into `vips_buf_vappendf()`, where `vips_vsnprintf`/`printf_common` re-reads the freed string. The saved ASan trace reports `heap-use-after-free READ of size 2` at `libvips/iofuncs/buf.c:418`, with the free at `libvips/foreign/matrixload.c:239`. The staged patch fixes this exact lifetime bug by moving `g_free(line)` after `vips_error(...)`. Stage 02 did not execute the fixed image.

source.description: First project-side statement on the crashing row that materializes attacker-controlled row bytes into vulnerability-relevant heap state. After the valid matrix header has admitted this loader, `vips_sbuf_get_line_copy()` copies the current untrusted data row into heap buffer `line`.
source.value_from:
The staged `poc` is a 27-byte matrix-text witness (sha256 `3cfcbc8d42403212d70c812ce920660b77297659cf31e09b5753dfe5a7f1356f`) that begins with header bytes `31 20 39 0a` (`1 9
`). After that admitted header, later data rows in the same file include one-token non-digit lines such as `0xc0
` and `0x12
`; on the crashing iteration, `vips_sbuf_get_line_copy()` reads one such row into `line`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: ASan-observed sink. The error formatter expands `bad number "%s"` with the dangling token pointer forwarded from `matrixload`, so `vips_vsnprintf` dereferences freed row-buffer bytes while formatting the `%s` argument.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `heap-use-after-free READ of size 2` at `libvips/iofuncs/buf.c:418` in `vips_buf_vappendf`, with frame 0 in `printf_common` and the freeing call at `libvips/foreign/matrixload.c:239`.

root_cause.description: The parser frees the row buffer before reporting the conversion error. Because `p` still aliases the current token inside `line`, the subsequent `vips_error(..., p)` call uses a dangling pointer. The staged fix removes this use-after-free by moving `g_free(line)` after `vips_error(...)`.

tainted_value_origin.code: for( x = 0, p = line; (q = vips_break_token( p, " \t" )) && x < load->out->Xsize; x++, p = q )
tainted_value_origin.description: The current data-row token pointer `p` is made to alias the heap buffer returned by `vips_sbuf_get_line_copy()`. That alias is the exact value later propagated through `vips_error()` after `line` has already been freed.

parser_admitted.description: The first line of the staged witness is `1 9`, so `parse_matrix_header()` succeeds and admits the file to the matrix loader. The same header path initializes output dimensions `width = 1` and `height = 9`, which makes the later row loop parse exactly one token per row.

fine_trace.note: Source. On the crashing row, `matrixload` copies the current attacker-controlled data line from `matrix->sbuf` into a fresh heap buffer. The admitted header has already fixed `load->out->Xsize = 1`, so this row will be parsed as a single token.

fine_trace.code: for( x = 0, p = line; (q = vips_break_token( p, " \t" )) && x < load->out->Xsize; x++, p = q )
fine_trace.note: The loop initializes `p = line` and tokenizes the copied row in place. Because the current row holds only one token and `load->out->Xsize = 1`, this iteration keeps `p` pointing directly into the heap buffer from step 1.

The current row token contains no digit on the crashing path, so `vips_strtod()` returns `-1` and control enters the bad-number error branch. No duplicate copy of the token text is created before that branch is taken.

Root cause. The row buffer is freed before the error message is formatted. `p` still aliases bytes inside `line`, so this statement turns the current token pointer into a dangling pointer. The staged fix moves this free below `vips_error(...)`.

Immediately after step 4, the error path passes the dangling token pointer as the `%s` argument for the bad-number message. That stale pointer is forwarded unchanged through `vips_error()` and `vips_verror()` into the formatter.

Sink. `vips_verror()` calls `vips_buf_vappendf()` with format `bad number "%s"` and varargs containing the dangling pointer from step 5. `vips_vsnprintf()` and the ASan top frame `printf_common` dereference that freed string while expanding `%s`, and the saved trace reports a heap-use-after-free READ of size 2 at this line.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged fix moves `g_free(line)` from before to after `vips_error(class->nickname, _( "bad number \"%s\"" ), p)` in `vips_foreign_load_matrix_load()`, so the `%s` formatter no longer receives a dangling token pointer. Stage 02 did not execute the fixed image.

format.name: libvips matrix text file
format.contract: The verified trigger semantics are limited to the exact staged 27-byte witness `poc` (sha256 `3cfcbc8d42403212d70c812ce920660b77297659cf31e09b5753dfe5a7f1356f`) interpreted by `vips_image_new_from_file()` as a matrix text file. The first line must remain a valid matrix header `1 9\n` so `matrixload` is selected and `vips_foreign_load_matrix_header()` admits `width = 1` and `height = 9`. A later one-token data row must still contain no digit, so `vips_strtod()` takes the bad-number error path while `p` still aliases the heap line buffer. The preserved artifacts do not justify a broader contract than witnesses preserving that admitted matrix-header state and a later bad-number row on this loader.
